Experimental results show that, at 128 sessions per generation on four added HBF sites, Mayfly finishes 34% sooner than parking the same KV on HBF and 23% sooner than reading it from HBF whenever HBM is full
CLM-MEM-0061.statement: At 128 sessions per generation on four added HBF sites, Mayfly finishes 23% sooner than reading KV from HBF whenever HBM is full.

extra_quotes: We evaluate Mayfly on real agent traces and recorded RSI runs in a discrete-event simulator whose GPU model is calibrated against an H200 and whose HBF path is modelled.

A discrete-event simulator re-implements vLLM’s block pool, scheduler and preemption, with step time and energy fitted on H200 replays, one of which spills KV to host DRAM (within 0.5%); on a held-out replay with a 20 GB KV pool, it is within 0.9% of the measured run time, 1.6% of the energy and 5% of the preemptions.
The specification leaves energy and array timing open, so we take 20 and 100 pJ/bit for reads and writes and 20 𝜇s page reads from the high end of prior estimates [13, 28, 58, 65].
